sub_problems.why: Measured 2026-11-23 on akiendelllinux (cairn e0c2b62ac): bare_temp_reach named bin/proofs/test_delete_gate.py:187, a measured shell command held in a string. Its one consumer is `for command in measured: assert gate.verdict(command) is None` (:193), and bin/cmd/deletegate has no subprocess, exec, eval, Popen or os.system call site. So it is data the delete gate judges, not a reach, yet it reds scratch's corpus tooth and bin's own (red tickets 0746da231128, a30a49e8631f, e3b9eef2fc1e). The scan reads strings on purpose: 008baf08f4d8's reach was a child script's text (248a29f29^, the git-env proof line 46), written with write_text and run with subprocess. The file test_delete_gate.py does call subprocess (:286-305, the gate run on a JSON payload), so a per-file 'has a sink' rule cannot tell the two apart; the rule must follow each string.
